assumptions: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure. Completeness is derived.
\(P\) is a probability measure on \(E\times\mathbb R\), and its first-coordinate pushforward is exactly \(\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\).

\(S=\{w:\|w\|=1\}\). The display defines the literal predictor \(f_\mu\), potential \(V_\mu\), projection \(G_\mu\), and cost \(c(w,u)=\arccos\langle w,u\rangle\).

steps.title: Transfer the existing conclusions to the literal potential
steps.text: Take scalar-potential integrability and the actual ambient gradient from the representation producer. Replace the projected adjoint expression by \(G\) in the feature-law conclusions for both laws. This yields the original tangency, norm and angular transport statements without changing their constants or their scope. The formal square root is the real value of the extended-nonnegative power \(Q^{1/2}\); the parent also proves \(Q<\infty\).

units.lean_statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, let γ=stdGaussian(E) be its centered standard identity-covariance Gaussian, and let S={w in E: norm(w)=1}. Let P be a probability law on E×ℝ with first marginal γ, p a finite real polynomial, and the actual response (x,y)↦y square-integrable under P. For each parameter probability μ on S, define f_μ(x)=∫_S p(inner(w,x))dμ(w), V_μ(w)=2∫(f_μ(x)−y)p(inner(w,x))dP(x,y), g_μ(w)=gradient(V_μ)(w), and G_μ(w)=g_μ(w)−inner(g_μ(w),w)w. For w,u in S define c(w,u)=arccos(inner(w,u)); let Π(μ,ν) be all probability measures on S×S with marginals μ,ν, and Q(μ,ν)=inf_{π in Π(μ,ν)}∫c²dπ, an extended nonnegative cost. Then the integrand defining V_μ is integrable at every ambient weight and its actual ambient gradient exists there. There are positive C₁,C₂, chosen before all parameter laws and unit weights, such that G_μ(w) is tangent, norm(G_μ(w))≤C₁, Q(μ,ν) is finite, and norm(G_μ(w)−G_ν(u))≤C₂(sqrt(Q(μ,ν))+c(w,u)). No independence of response/input or derivative, domination, mean-bound, integral-identity or gradient oracle is assumed. Constants may depend on E,p,P, including the response L² norm. The theorem concerns the explicit angular cost and projected ambient gradient; it does not assert an intrinsic path-length identity, an installed manifold-gradient/Wasserstein API, teacher/noise construction or full model convergence.
